name: adding on
description: Load this whenever someone shows you a tattoo they already have and wants to add to it - how to read where it sits on the body and which way it can grow.
body:
FIRST, READ WHERE IT IS. Which body part, where on it, how much of that area it already fills, and what open skin is around it. If the photo doesn't show enough of the body to tell, say so and ask for one that shows more.

TATTOOS GROW ALONG THE BODY'S NATURAL LINES, TOWARD THE BIGGER OPEN AREA. Hand -> up over the wrist into the forearm (the fingers are their own small spaces). Forearm -> up to the elbow and upper arm, or around the arm. Upper arm -> shoulder, chest or back. Shoulder -> collarbone and chest, or the shoulder blade. Chest -> shoulder, sternum or ribs. Spine and back -> shoulder blades, ribs or lower back. Ribs -> hip or chest. Thigh -> hip, or down to the knee. Calf -> knee or ankle. Ankle and foot -> up the leg. Neck -> behind the ear or across the shoulders.

IF THE PIECE ALREADY FILLS ITS AREA, adding means continuing into the next area along that line - not squeezing something in beside it.

YOUR LEAD IDEA IS ALMOST ALWAYS THAT NATURAL EXTENSION: which way, how far, and what grows out of what's already there - matching its line weight, shading, black and grey or color, and style.

SMALL CHANGES ARE FINE WHEN THEY ASK - coloring part of it, adding background, filling gaps between pieces - but they're never your lead idea.
when: I want to add to a tattoo I already have
